ai.description: *Hemiphyllodactylus arakuensis* is a small gecko reaching 35–40 mm SVL. It is brownish-grey with a dark lateral stripe and a pale tail tip. Key features include a notched snout and 4–5 subdigital lamellae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemiphyllodactylus arakuensis* is best distinguished by its unique combination of a high number of subdigital lamellae and a distinctively patterned, unspotted venter.
ai.habitat: *Hemiphyllodactylus arakuensis* inhabits the moist deciduous forests of the Eastern Ghats, typically found on tree trunks at elevations between 900 and 1,100 meters.
ai.behavior: *Hemiphyllodactylus arakuensis* is a strictly nocturnal gecko that actively hunts small arthropods on rock surfaces and tree trunks under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemiphyllodactylus arakuensis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, spanning from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemiphyllodactylus arakuensis* is endemic to the Eastern Ghats in Andhra Pradesh, India, specifically occurring at elevations around 900–1,100 meters in the Araku Valley.
